notes: Single L4x4x1/4 A36 angle, 15-1/2 in long, with 5 rows of 3/4 in A325-N (threads included) snug-tight bolts at 3 in pitch in standard holes through the W24x55 web and the W14x61 flange. Ra = 39.449 kip (ASD). Hand check to AISC 360-22: angle block shear, both legs, 0.85 (Ubs = 1, tension plane to the toe). Angle shear rupture 0.82. Both bolt groups were taken as eccentric (ICR, Manual Part 7): support leg e = 2.25 + tw/2 = 2.45 in, C = 4.18; beam-web leg e = 2.25 in, C = 4.28. The bolt-group check used C times the smallest single-bolt strength, including end and toe tearout on the 1/4 in angle (11.7 kip per bolt), giving 0.81. Bolt shear alone is 0.79. Angle shear yield 0.71; shear plus flexure interaction 0.79; flexural yield and rupture about 0.34. Beam-web bearing, column-flange bearing and beam shear are all at or below 0.6. Detailing: Lev 1.75 in, toe edges 1.75 in, beam edge 1.75 in as detailed (1.5 in for strength after the 1/4 in underrun), setback 1/2 in, angle top 1-3/4 in below the beam top (clear of the flange fillet), and angle length 15.5 in, between T/2 and T. The column bolt line is 2.45 in from the column centreline, which clears the web fillet, and the 4 in outstanding leg stays inside the 10 in flange. This assumes the beam web is centred on the column flange. Gauges of 2-1/4 in are slightly less than the usual 2-1/2 in for a 4 in leg. That was chosen so the toe edges reach 1-3/4 in, and it leaves entering and tightening clearance for 3/4 in bolts. Not checked by petra (unavailable); utilisation is from this hand calculation.
